name: Project scaffolding and dependencies
description: Set up the project so `main.py` starts a local Flask web server. Add Flask, numpy, scipy, matplotlib, and pytest as dependencies via `uv add` (do not use pip/conda). Create the package layout for the stats engine (e.g. `h2h/stats.py`) separate from the web layer (e.g. `h2h/app.py`), with `main.py` at the repo root simply importing and running the Flask app. Running `uv run main.py` must start the server and serve a placeholder page at `/`.
tests: `uv run main.py` starts without error and binds to a localhost port.
A GET request to `/` returns HTTP 200.
The stats module can be imported independently of Flask (`import h2h.stats` succeeds with Flask not running).

name: Per-arrow score PMF from handicap
description: In the stats engine, implement a function that takes an AGB handicap and an `archeryutils.targets.Target`, and returns the full per-arrow score probability mass function (a mapping of score value to probability), derived from `sigma_r(handicap, distance)` and the target's `face_spec`, using the same ring-probability terms `archeryutils` computes internally for `HandicapScheme.arrow_score`/`_s_bar`. Must not duplicate `archeryutils`'s scoring-system logic beyond what is necessary to expose the per-ring probabilities instead of just their mean.
tests: For a range of handicaps (e.g. 0, 10, 25, 50, 80) and at least two target faces, the PMF's probabilities sum to 1 (within floating point tolerance).
For the same inputs, the PMF's expected value (`sum(score * prob)`) matches `archeryutils`'s `HandicapScheme.arrow_score(handicap, target)` within floating point tolerance.
All PMF probabilities are >= 0.

name: n_pass score distribution via convolution
description: Implement a function that takes a per-arrow PMF (from task 2) and an integer `n_pass`, and returns the exact probability distribution of the summed score over `n_pass` arrows, computed via discrete self-convolution (not Monte Carlo, not a Gaussian/CLT approximation).
tests: For n_pass in {1, 6, 12, 60}, the resulting distribution's probabilities sum to 1 (within floating point tolerance).
The resulting distribution's expected value equals `n_pass * arrow_score(handicap, target)` within floating point tolerance.
For n_pass = 1, the result is identical to the input per-arrow PMF.

name: Percentile computation and pass-winner decision
description: Implement a function that, given an n_pass score distribution (from task 3) and an archer's actual observed pass score, returns that archer's percentile (the probability of scoring at or below the observed score under their own distribution). Implement a second function that takes two archers' percentiles (plus their raw scores, for tie-breaking) and returns the pass winner, using the tie-break rule: equal percentile -> higher raw score wins; still equal -> coin flip.
tests: Percentile values returned are always in [0, 1].
An archer scoring the minimum possible score for their distribution gets a percentile at or near 0; scoring the maximum possible gets a percentile at or near 1.
Given two different percentiles, the winner-decision function picks the higher one.
Given equal percentiles but different raw scores, the winner-decision function picks the higher raw score.

Given equal percentiles and equal raw scores, the winner-decision function still returns a valid winner (does not error or hang) and this is verified as a genuine coin flip (not always the same archer) across repeated calls.

name: Match/round data model and orchestration
description: Implement `Archer`, `Pass`, `Match`, and `Round` data structures per AISpec.md §6. `Round` should source its target/distance/arrow-count metadata from `archeryutils.load_rounds` (default: Portsmouth). `Match` should compute the number of passes as `60 / n_pass` and reject non-divisor `n_pass` values. Provide a function to record a pass's scores for both archers (computing percentiles and pass winner via tasks 2-4) and a function to compute the overall match result (majority of passes wins; even split is a draw) once all passes are recorded.
tests: Creating a `Match` with an `n_pass` that does not divide 60 evenly raises a clear error.
For n_pass = 12, a `Match` has exactly 5 passes.
Recording pass scores for both archers correctly updates the running per-archer pass-win tally.
A match where one archer wins a strict majority of passes reports that archer as the overall winner.
A match with an even pass count and an even split of pass wins reports a draw.

name: Match setup UI (archer entry, pairing, n_pass slider)
description: Build the setup page: form to add archers (name, handicap, optional bowstyle label), automatic sequential pairing into matches, and a slider restricted to the divisors of 60 ({1,2,3,4,5,6,10,12,15,20,30,60}, default 12) to set `n_pass` for the session before scoring starts. Submitting creates the in-memory `Match` objects for the session.
tests: Adding an odd number of archers flags the last one as unpaired and excludes them from scoring, without crashing the app.
The n_pass slider cannot be set to a value that is not a divisor of 60 (UI prevents it, or server-side validation rejects it with a clear error).
Submitting valid archer data creates one Match per pair with the chosen n_pass.

name: Pass score entry and live results (basic mode)
description: Build the basic-mode scoring page: for each match, one input box per archer for the current pass's total score. On submission, display that pass's winner and the running match score (passes won so far by each archer), and progress to the next pass. After the final pass, display the overall match result (winner or draw) per task 5.
tests: Entering both archers' scores for a pass and submitting displays a pass winner consistent with the stats engine's decision (task 4) for those inputs.
The running match score displayed after each pass matches the tally computed by the Match object.
After the final pass of a match, the overall match result shown matches the Match object's computed result.

name: Basic/Advanced UI toggle
description: Add a visible, session-wide toggle switching between basic mode (task 7 only) and advanced mode (task 9). Toggling must not lose any already-entered scores or match progress.
tests: Toggling from basic to advanced mode and back preserves all previously entered pass scores and running results.
The toggle state is visually clear (unambiguous which mode is active).

name: Advanced mode: distribution plots and maths explanation
description: In advanced mode, for each scored pass, render (via matplotlib, as a static image) each archer's handicap-implied n_pass score distribution with their actual score and resulting percentile marked. Also display a short, human-readable explanation of the underlying method (summarising AISpec.md §2: handicap -> sigma_r -> per-arrow PMF -> convolved n_pass distribution -> percentile comparison), including the explicit note that the bowstyle-variance correction is not applied in this version.
tests: For a scored pass, an image is rendered showing both archers' distributions with their observed scores marked.
The maths explanation text is present and mentions that bowstyle-variance correction is not applied.
Advanced-mode content does not appear when the toggle (task 8) is set to basic mode.

name: End-to-end integration check
description: Write an integration test (or documented manual test procedure, if automated browser testing is out of scope) that runs a full session end to end: add archers with differing handicaps, set n_pass, enter all pass scores for a match, and confirm the displayed overall match result matches an independently hand-calculated expectation for at least one concrete worked example (e.g. using the mean-only comparison as a sanity check that the favoured archer's percentile calculation is directionally correct).
tests: A full session (setup through final match result) completes without error for at least 2 archers and one full round of passes.
The final displayed result for the worked example matches the independently computed expectation.
Restarting the app clears all prior match state (confirms no unintended persistence, per Assumption 7).

name: Pass score validation and integer display
description: Per Specification/feedback.md 'Feedback 1': a pass score over n_pass arrows must be a whole number in [0, n_pass * MAX_SCORE_PER_ARROW], with MAX_SCORE_PER_ARROW hard-coded to 10. Reject invalid input (non-integer, negative, above the maximum, or non-numeric) with a specific, human-readable error message instead of a 500 or silent acceptance, without recording anything. Recorded scores must always display as plain integers (no trailing '.0').
tests: A negative score is rejected with a message naming the valid range.
A score above n_pass * 10 is rejected with a message naming the valid range.
A non-integer score (e.g. 100.5) is rejected with a 'whole number' message.
Non-numeric input (e.g. 'abc') is rejected with a clear message, not a 500.
0 and n_pass * 10 (the inclusive boundaries) are accepted.
A recorded score renders without a trailing '.0' in the match page.

name: Per-pass equivalent handicap
description: Add a full-round-equivalent AGB handicap column per archer per pass: the handicap that would, on average, produce that archer's actual pass score, computed via archeryutils's own handicap_from_score rootfinder over a one-off Round built from n_pass arrows at the match's target. Undefined (displayed as '-') for a score of 0.
tests: A nonzero pass score gets a recorded equivalent handicap for both archers.
A zero pass score has an undefined (None) equivalent handicap.
A lower pass score implies a numerically larger (worse) AGB handicap than a higher pass score.
The equivalent-handicap column is visible in the match page's pass table once a pass is scored.

name: Interactive single-graph distribution chart
description: Replace the per-pass static matplotlib PNG charts with one interactive chart per match (Chart.js via a pinned CDN version): both archers' n_pass score distributions as smoothed, shaded curves on one shared graph, trimmed to a sensible x-range (not the full achievable score range) rather than two separate discretised bar charts. Hovering shows both archers' current probability values at that score. Each scored pass's actual scores are marked as vertical lines; only the most recent pass's markers are shown by default, with a checkbox to reveal every previous pass's markers too.
tests: h2h.chart_data.build_match_chart_data returns a payload with both archers' distribution points, a shared x_min/x_max range narrower than the full 0..n_pass*10 range for two differently-skilled archers, and a y_max ceiling.
The x-range still gets a sensible minimum width for a near-zero-variance distribution (e.g. two handicap-0 archers), even though its mean sits at the edge of the achievable range.
Every distribution point falls within the reported x-range.
Scored passes appear in the payload in order with their raw scores; no scored passes gives an empty list.
The match page in advanced mode renders a canvas#match-chart, embeds the chart payload as window.MATCH_CHART_DATA, and does not render either in basic mode.

UPDATE: subsequently verified in a real headless-Edge browser (via an ephemeral Selenium install) during Feedback 2 processing -- confirmed the chart renders two curve datasets, the checkbox correctly adds/removes prior passes' marker datasets (verified via Chart.js's own dataset list and a screenshot), and no JS console errors occur (aside from an unrelated favicon 404).

name: Subscript typesetting for underscore identifiers
description: Any underscore-separated identifier shown in user-facing text (n_pass, sigma_r) must be typeset with a proper subscript (n<sub>pass</sub>, sigma<sub>r</sub>) instead of displaying the literal underscore. Error messages that would otherwise need to show such an identifier are reworded to avoid it instead, since plain-text error strings can't carry markup.
tests: The setup page renders 'n<sub>pass</sub>' and not a literal 'n_pass' label.
No user-facing template text contains a literal 'n_pass' or 'sigma_r' outside of Jinja value expressions (verified by grep across h2h/templates).
The invalid-n_pass error message is reworded to avoid the raw identifier.

name: Round-robin rotation scheduler
description: Add h2h/rotation.py: a Flask- and stats-independent module generating a round-robin ('circle method') rotation schedule over n_archers positions (0..n_archers-1) for a requested number of rotations. Odd n_archers gets a bye slot each rotation (one archer index with no opponent that rotation). If requested rotations < a full round-robin's length, truncate; if more, cycle the schedule from the start to fill the rest (Specification/AISpec.md Assumption 13).
tests: For even n_archers, a full-length schedule has every archer paired with every other archer exactly once across n_archers-1 rotations, and no archer has a bye.
For odd n_archers, a full-length schedule has n_archers rotations, each with exactly one archer on the bye, and every archer has exactly one bye across the full schedule.
No rotation pairs an archer with themselves, and no archer appears twice (as two different opponents) within the same rotation.
Requesting fewer rotations than a full round-robin needs returns a truncated prefix of the full schedule.
Requesting more rotations than a full round-robin needs repeats the schedule from the start for the extra rotations.
n_archers=2 produces a single rotation with one pair and no bye.

name: Per-archer target resolution (round mode x bowstyle)
description: Add a function resolving an archer's effective archeryutils Target from the event's round mode (indoor+Portsmouth/WA18, or outdoor) and the archer's bowstyle, per Specification/AISpec.md section 5.2a: indoor Compound uses the *_compound scoring-system variant (portsmouth_compound / wa18_compound) of the same face/distance; indoor Recurve/Barebow use the plain variant; outdoor uses one single fixed target (AISpec.md Assumption 12: wa720_70's target) for every bowstyle.
tests: Indoor Portsmouth + Compound resolves to portsmouth_compound's target (same diameter/distance as portsmouth, scoring_system '10_zone_compound').
Indoor Portsmouth + Recurve or Barebow resolves to portsmouth's own target ('10_zone').
Indoor WA18 + Compound resolves to wa18_compound's target; + Recurve/Barebow resolves to wa18's target.
Outdoor mode resolves to the same fixed target regardless of bowstyle (Recurve, Compound, and Barebow all get an identical Target).
The resolved target's `indoor` flag is correct in each case (True for both indoor rounds, False for outdoor), so per_arrow_pmf's automatic arrow-diameter selection is unaffected.

name: Event data model (replaces fixed-pair Match)
description: Add h2h.models.Event, Rotation, and result-tracking structures per Specification/AISpec.md section 6, replacing the old single-pair Match for new code (existing Match-based tests/routes are migrated in later tasks, not kept alongside). Event holds archers, total_arrows, n_pass, round_mode, the rotation schedule (task 15), and each archer's own precomputed n_pass score distribution (handicap + task-16-resolved target, independent of opponent). Provides recording a rotation's scores (validating each score per the existing MAX_SCORE_PER_ARROW rule), computing each archer's percentile/equivalent handicap for that pass, deciding each pair's pass winner, and maintaining a running pairwise result (win/loss/draw) per pair of archers who have shared at least one rotation.
tests: Constructing an Event with n_archers/total_arrows/n_pass computes a schedule of total_arrows // n_pass rotations via task 15.
Recording a rotation's scores for all its pairs (and bye archer, if any) computes each participant's percentile and equivalent handicap using their OWN resolved target/distribution, not a shared one.
A bye archer's pass is recorded (score + percentile) but produces no winner and does not appear in any pairwise result.
After a pair shares one pass, querying that pair's pairwise result returns a win/loss based on that pass's winner.
If a pair shares multiple passes (schedule cycling, task 15), their pairwise result aggregates across all shared passes (majority; even split is a draw), mirroring the old Match.result() semantics.
Invalid scores (non-integer, out of range) are rejected via the same validation as before, leaving the rotation unrecorded.
Two archers with different bowstyles under indoor mode get correctly different target-based distributions (task 16 wired through).

name: Stage 1 setup UI (event configuration)
description: Build the Stage 1 page per Specification/AISpec.md section 5.1: n_archers (integer, >=2), total_arrows (default 60), n_pass (snap control restricted to divisors of the CHOSEN total_arrows, not a fixed set), round mode (indoor -> Portsmouth/WA18 sub-choice, or outdoor). Submitting validates inputs, builds the rotation schedule (task 15) over n_archers positions, stores it in session state, and proceeds to Stage 2 (task 19) with exactly n_archers archer-detail rows expected.
tests: Submitting valid Stage 1 inputs stores a schedule with the correct number of rotations and redirects to Stage 2.
n_pass values that don't divide the chosen total_arrows are rejected server-side with a clear error, re-rendering Stage 1 without crashing.
Changing total_arrows changes which n_pass values are offered/accepted (e.g. total_arrows=40 accepts n_pass=8 but not n_pass=12).
n_archers < 2 is rejected with a clear error.
Selecting indoor requires (and outdoor omits) the Portsmouth/WA18 sub-choice in the submitted form.

name: Stage 2 setup UI (archer details)
description: Build the Stage 2 page per Specification/AISpec.md section 5.2: exactly n_archers rows (from Stage 1, not a generic fixed count) collecting name, bowstyle (dropdown: Recurve/Compound/Barebow, required), and handicap. Submitting binds these Archers to the Stage 1 schedule's positions in entry order and constructs the Event (task 17), then proceeds to the rotation-scoring view (task 20).
tests: Stage 2 renders exactly n_archers rows, matching whatever n_archers was chosen in Stage 1.
Submitting valid archer details for all rows creates an Event and redirects to the rotation-scoring view.
A missing or invalid bowstyle value is rejected with a clear error (dropdown only offers the three valid values).
Attempting to reach Stage 2 without having completed Stage 1 redirects back to Stage 1 instead of erroring.

name: Rotation scoring UI
description: Build the per-rotation scoring page per Specification/AISpec.md section 5.3: for the event's current (first not-fully-scored) rotation, show one score-entry box per archer in each pair (grouped by pair) plus a single box for the bye archer's score if there is one that rotation. Submitting records all of that rotation's scores via Event (task 17) in one action and advances to the next rotation (or shows event-complete state once every rotation is scored).
tests: The scoring page for a rotation shows exactly the right set of input boxes: one pair per matched pair, plus the bye archer's single box if n_archers is odd that rotation.
Submitting a rotation's scores for all pairs (and bye, if present) records them and advances next_pass_index()-equivalent to the following rotation.
An invalid score anywhere in the submitted rotation is rejected with a specific error and does not partially record the rotation.
After the final rotation is scored, the page indicates the event is complete rather than prompting for another rotation.

name: Per-pass and pairwise results display
description: Display both result levels from Specification/AISpec.md section 5.4: a per-rotation table of every scored pass (score/percentile/equivalent handicap per archer, winner if paired), and a pairwise-results view listing every pair of archers who have shared at least one rotation with their aggregated win/loss/draw -- explicitly NOT a ranked leaderboard across all archers (out of scope).
tests: After scoring a rotation, the per-pass table shows that rotation's results for every participant, matching the Event object's recorded PassResults.
The pairwise-results view shows an entry for every pair that has shared a rotation so far, with the correct win/loss/draw, and no entry for pairs that haven't met yet.
The pairwise-results view does not compute or display any single ranked score/points total across all archers.

name: Static handicap conversion tool
description: Add a standalone page/route per Specification/AISpec.md section 5.5: pick Portsmouth or WA18, enter a full-round score, see the resulting AGB handicap to 1 decimal place, computed via archeryutils's real Portsmouth/WA18 Round objects (not a synthetic partial round). Reachable from Stage 2 and independently from the nav at any time; its result is never stored against any archer or wired into the event.
tests: Submitting a valid Portsmouth score returns the correct handicap to 1 decimal place, matching archeryutils.handicaps.handicap_scheme('AGB').handicap_from_score directly on the real Portsmouth round.
Submitting a valid WA18 score returns the correct handicap similarly against the real WA18 round.
An out-of-range or non-numeric score shows a friendly error instead of a 500.
The tool is reachable from the nav independent of where the scorer currently is in event setup/scoring.

name: Adapt advanced-mode charts to per-pair-with-shared-history
description: Update h2h/chart_data.py and the advanced-mode UI to build a distribution chart for each pair of archers who have shared at least one rotation (per Specification/AISpec.md section 5.6), rather than one fixed match's two archers. Each archer's distribution now comes from their own resolved target (task 16), not a shared match target. Preserve the existing behaviour verified for Feedback 1: trimmed x-range, shared y-axis, only-latest-pass markers by default with a checkbox for all shared passes.
tests: build_match_chart_data (or its Event-based equivalent) produces a valid payload for any pair that has shared at least one rotation, using each archer's own distribution.
Two archers with different resolved targets (e.g. different bowstyles indoors) get visibly different distribution curves in the payload.
No chart payload/canvas is generated for a pair that hasn't shared a rotation yet.
Re-verify in a real browser (per the working method established for task 13) that the checkbox still correctly toggles prior shared passes' markers under the new per-pair data source.

name: Retire the old fixed-pair setup/scoring routes and migrate tests
description: Remove the old single-stage setup page and fixed-pair Match-based routes/templates now superseded by tasks 18-21, and update/replace the existing test suite (tests/test_app.py, tests/test_models.py, tests/test_integration.py, tests/test_chart_data.py) to exercise the new two-stage, rotation-based flow instead. Do not leave dead/unreachable old routes or templates behind.
tests: No route still references the old single-pair Match model or the old one-stage setup form.
The full test suite passes with no references to the removed Match-based routes/behaviour.
Grep confirms no leftover dead template files or unused imports from the old flow.

name: End-to-end integration check for the rotation flow
description: Write an integration test exercising the full new flow end to end: Stage 1 -> Stage 2 -> score every rotation -> confirm per-pass and pairwise results are correct, for both an even and an odd n_archers case (covering bye handling), and for both indoor (with mixed bowstyles) and outdoor round modes.
tests: Even n_archers: full event completes, every archer's pairwise results match the expected round-robin coverage (everyone faces everyone once, given enough rotations).
Odd n_archers: each rotation has exactly one bye archer whose pass is recorded with no winner, and byes are distributed as the scheduler intends.

Indoor mode with a mix of Compound and Recurve/Barebow archers: verify (via h2h.stats/h2h.models directly, as an independent check) that the Compound archer's recorded equivalent handicap/percentile used the compound-scoring target, not the plain one.
Outdoor mode: all archers use the same fixed target regardless of bowstyle.
Restarting the app (fresh SessionState) clears all event state, consistent with Assumption 7.

name: Add Longbow to the bowstyle dropdown
description: Per Specification/feedback.md 'Feedback 3' and Specification/AISpec.md section 5.2/5.2a (Assumption 18): add Longbow as a fourth Bowstyle. It resolves to the same targets as Recurve/Barebow (plain indoor scoring, the single fixed outdoor target) and never affects sigma_r. Stage 2's bowstyle dropdown offers it, and the Bowstyle docstring no longer claims there are only three.
tests: Bowstyle has a Longbow member with value 'Longbow', alongside Recurve, Compound and Barebow.
resolve_target gives Longbow the plain target (scoring system '10_zone', identical to Recurve's) for both indoor Portsmouth and indoor WA18.
Outdoor mode resolves Longbow to the same fixed target as every other bowstyle.
Two archers with the same handicap, one Recurve and one Longbow, get identical score distributions in an indoor event.
The Stage 2 page offers 'Longbow' in every row's bowstyle dropdown, and submitting a Longbow archer starts the event.

name: Compound option in the handicap calculator
description: Per Specification/feedback.md 'Feedback 3' and Specification/AISpec.md section 5.5 (Assumption 19): the standalone score-to-handicap calculator gains a Yes/No 'compound bow' checkbox (default No). Compound uses archeryutils's portsmouth_compound / wa18_compound round (same face and distance, only the X-ring scores 10), non-compound the plain round. Reuse the round-selection logic that resolve_target already uses for indoor compound rounds rather than duplicating it. The result is still never stored against an archer.
tests: A Portsmouth score with compound ticked returns the handicap archeryutils computes on portsmouth_compound, to 1 decimal place, and this differs from the non-compound result for the same score.
A WA 18 score with compound ticked returns the handicap archeryutils computes on wa18_compound, to 1 decimal place.
Submitting without the compound field behaves exactly as before (plain rounds), so existing calculator behaviour is unchanged.
An invalid or non-numeric score with compound ticked still shows a friendly error, not a 500.
The calculator page renders a compound control.
resolve_target's indoor round selection and the calculator share one code path (no duplicated compound/non-compound round lookup).

name: Scheduler: sitting-out rotations and the no-bye-shot schedule
description: Extend h2h/rotation.py per Specification/AISpec.md section 5.3 (Assumption 15). Add a `sitting_out: tuple[int, ...] = ()` field and a `matches` property (pairs, then the bye archer's solo match as (archer, None)) to Rotation; existing build_schedule behaviour is unchanged. Add build_sit_out_schedule(n_archers, passes_per_archer) for an odd n_archers whose bye archers do not shoot: run the cycling round-robin for the largest number of rotations in which no archer would exceed passes_per_archer passes (each rotation's bye archer sits out), then, if any archers are exactly one pass short, add one catch-up rotation pairing those archers with each other (preferring opponents not yet faced; if their number is odd, add one already-complete archer as a partner) with everyone else sitting out. For an even n_archers it simply returns build_schedule(n_archers, passes_per_archer).
tests: Rotation.matches lists the pairs followed by (bye, None) when there is a bye, and just the pairs otherwise; existing build_schedule tests still pass unchanged.
For odd n_archers in 3..9 and passes_per_archer in 1..12, every archer shoots at least passes_per_archer passes, at most one archer shoots passes_per_archer + 1, and nobody shoots more than that.

Known cases: 5 archers needing 4 passes -> 5 rotations, everyone exactly 4; 5 archers needing 5 -> 7 rotations; 3 archers needing 5 -> 8 rotations; 3 archers needing 1 -> 2 rotations; 7 archers needing 5 -> 6 rotations.

Every rotation lists each non-shooting archer in sitting_out, has no `bye`, never schedules an archer twice or against themselves, and sitting_out plus matched archers cover every archer exactly once.
The catch-up rotation (when present) contains only archers who were exactly one pass short, plus at most one already-complete partner.
When the catch-up rotation can avoid repeating an earlier opponent it does (checked on a case where that is possible).
An even n_archers returns exactly build_schedule(n_archers, passes_per_archer).
n_archers < 2 or passes_per_archer < 1 raises ValueError.

name: 'Shoot byes?' option at event setup
description: Per Specification/feedback.md 'Feedback 3' and Specification/AISpec.md section 5.1 (Assumptions 15, 16): Stage 1 shows a 'Shoot byes?' Yes/No control (default Yes) only when n_archers is odd. SessionState gains a shoot_byes field (default True, cleared by reset) and start_stage1 takes it: for an odd n_archers with shoot_byes False it builds the schedule with build_sit_out_schedule (task 28), otherwise exactly as before. The control's visibility follows the parity of the n_archers input live, via JS, and is hidden/ignored for even counts. Explanatory text notes that choosing No adds passes.
tests: start_stage1 with an odd n_archers and shoot_byes False stores a sit-out schedule (sitting_out populated, no bye shoots alone) with more rotations than total_arrows // n_pass where the rule requires it; shoot_byes True or an even n_archers is unchanged from before.
SessionState stores shoot_byes (default True) and reset() restores the default.
POSTing Stage 1 with shoot_byes=no and an odd n_archers stores False; with an even n_archers the field is ignored and the schedule is the ordinary one.
The Stage 1 page renders the Shoot byes? control and its explanatory text, and re-renders the previously chosen value.
Verified in a real browser: the control is hidden for an even n_archers, shown for an odd one, and updates live as the n_archers input changes, with no JS console errors.

name: Event: per-match score recording and explicit pass advance
description: Per Specification/AISpec.md sections 5.3/6 (Assumption 17): add to h2h.models.Event, alongside the existing record_rotation (which the web layer stops using in task 31, where it is then removed), the primitives the new page flow needs. `current_rotation_index` (starts 0, the pass being shot); matches(rotation_index) (delegating to Rotation.matches); record_match(scores) which records one match of the current rotation from a {archer_index: score} dict covering exactly one pair or the solo bye archer, validating scores via the existing _validate_score, computing percentile/equivalent handicap/winner exactly as record_rotation does (factor the shared logic out rather than copying it), and replacing earlier results for those archers in that rotation in place if the match was already scored; is_match_scored / is_rotation_complete; and advance(), which moves to the next rotation only once the current one is complete. Event construction should also bounds-check archer indices in sitting_out.
tests: A new Event starts at current_rotation_index 0.
record_match on one pair records percentile, equivalent handicap and winner using each archer's OWN distribution, without any other match of the rotation being scored.
record_match on the bye archer's solo match records a result with no opponent and no winner, and it never appears in any pairwise result.

record_match rejects a scores dict that is not exactly one match of the current rotation (an archer from a different match, a mismatched pair, an extra archer, a sitting-out archer) with ValueError, recording nothing.
An invalid score (non-integer, negative, above n_pass * 10) is rejected with the existing messages and records nothing.
Re-recording an already-scored match replaces its results (no duplicates), recomputes the winner, keeps results in a stable order, and the pairwise result reflects the replacement.
is_rotation_complete is False until every match of the rotation has results and True afterwards.

advance() raises ValueError while the current rotation is incomplete, and on the final rotation; otherwise it increments current_rotation_index and subsequent record_match calls apply to the new rotation.

name: Tie-break: percentile, then score, then closest to the middle (statistics and event model)
description: Per Specification/feedback.md 'Feedback 5' (Tie breaks) and Specification/AISpec.md section 5.3 'Tie-break' (Assumption 33): remove the random coin flip from the pass-winner decision. h2h.stats.decide_pass_winner no longer takes an rng. It compares percentiles (equal when their relative difference is below 1e-9), then raw scores, then an optional `closest` argument ('a' or 'b': the archer the scorer says was closest to the middle); it returns the winner ('a'/'b') together with which step decided it ('percentile', 'score' or 'closest'). If percentiles and scores are both tied and `closest` is not given it raises a dedicated ValueError subclass (TieBreakRequired) instead of guessing; an unneeded `closest` is ignored. PassResult gains `decided_by` (None for a bye match). Event.record_match accepts an optional `closest` archer index (which must be one of the two archers of the match) and passes it through; a tie with no closest archer raises TieBreakRequired and records nothing (earlier scores for the match stay untouched). Reopening a decided-by-closest match must be able to report which archer was ticked (the winner when decided_by == 'closest'). Update every existing test that relied on the coin flip or on the rng parameter.

Percentiles with a relative difference below 1e-9 (e.g. 1.0 and 1.0 - 1e-12, or 0.5 and 0.5 + 1e-12) count as equal, so the score decides; percentiles that differ by 1e-6 relative do not; two very small percentiles such as 1e-18 and 1e-20 are NOT tied (the higher wins by percentile); two exact zeros are tied.
Equal percentiles and equal scores with closest='a' or 'b' give that archer the win with decided_by 'closest'; with closest=None a TieBreakRequired (a ValueError) is raised.
A supplied `closest` is ignored when percentile or score already decides the pass (the winner and decided_by are unchanged).
decide_pass_winner no longer accepts an rng and nothing in h2h/ imports random for deciding a pass; the same inputs always give the same output (called 100 times).

Event.record_match on two archers with identical handicap, target and score and no closest raises TieBreakRequired and records nothing; the same call with closest=<one of the two archers> records both results with exactly one winner and decided_by 'closest'; a closest index that is not in the match raises ValueError.

Re-saving a tied match with a different closest archer replaces the earlier results (the other archer now wins); re-saving it with different scores that no longer tie ignores closest and stores decided_by 'percentile' or 'score'.
A bye match records decided_by None and a closest argument for it is ignored.
The full suite passes after the existing winner and tie tests are migrated.

name: Per-archer target setups and per-target maximum score (model)
description: Per Specification/feedback.md 'Feedback 5' (Advanced mode) and AISpec.md sections 5.2a and 6 (Assumptions 10, 34, 35): make the target an archer's own. TargetSetup gains an optional `face_type` (an archeryutils scoring system; None = chosen from the bowstyle as today). resolve_target uses face_type exactly as given when it is set (distance, face size and the indoor flag inferred from the archer's own distance as before) and is unchanged when it is None. Archer gains an optional `target_setup`; Event(archers, n_pass, target_setup, schedule) uses an archer's own setup if they have one, else the shared one, and accepts target_setup=None if every archer has their own (it raises ValueError otherwise). models.py defines the advanced-mode options: FACE_TYPES (every archeryutils scoring system except 'Custom', each with a readable name, in a sensible order, obtained from archeryutils itself so a future system is not silently missed), ADVANCED_FACE_SIZES_CM (20, 35, 40, 50, 60, 65, 80, 122) and a parse helper for per-archer form values that validates all three against the options. The highest score one arrow can earn is read from the resolved target (max of face_spec values) and replaces the hard-coded MAX_SCORE_PER_ARROW everywhere: Event exposes max_score_for(archer_index) (= n_pass * that maximum), record_match validates each score against its own archer's maximum, and the match page's score boxes use it for their max attribute and label. The statistics engine itself is unchanged.
tests: Every archeryutils scoring system except 'Custom' is in FACE_TYPES with a non-empty readable name, and nothing else is (compared with typing.get_args(ScoringSystem), so a library addition fails the test).

For every face type, face sizes {20, 40, 60, 122}, distances {18 m, 20 yd, 50 m, 100 yd} and handicaps {0, 50, 100, 150}, per_arrow_pmf sums to 1, is non-negative and has a mean equal to archeryutils's arrow_score; n_pass_score_distribution sums to 1 and its support is within [0, n_pass * max].

resolve_target with face_type set returns that scoring system, the setup's diameter and distance, and indoor from the distance, for every bowstyle (a Compound archer with face_type '10_zone' indoors gets plain '10_zone'; a Recurve archer with '10_zone_compound' gets the compound system); with face_type None it behaves exactly as before (existing target-resolution tests pass unchanged).

An Event whose archers each carry their own TargetSetup (target_setup=None) builds a distribution per archer from their own target: two same-handicap archers on different face types, sizes or distances get different distributions and target_for(i) returns each one's own target.
An archer's own setup overrides the shared one; an Event with target_setup=None and an archer lacking their own setup raises ValueError.

max_score_for is n_pass times 10 for 10_zone, 9 for 5_zone, 11 for 11_zone, 5 for Worcester and 1 for Beiter_hit_miss; record_match accepts the maximum and rejects one more for that archer, while accepting for another archer on a 10-zone face a score above the first archer's limit.
The match page's score box for an archer on a 5-zone face has max = n_pass * 9 and its label says so; boxes for 10-zone archers still say n_pass * 10.

The per-archer form-value parser accepts every offered (face type, size, distance) combination and rejects an unknown face type, a size not in the list and a non-standard distance with a message naming which value was wrong.
The full suite passes unchanged for simple setup (no existing event, state or route test needs editing except for the removed MAX_SCORE_PER_ARROW constant).

name: Advanced setup: per-archer face type, face size and distance
description: Per Specification/feedback.md 'Feedback 5' (Advanced mode) and AISpec.md sections 5.1 and 5.2 (Assumptions 30, 34): build the Stage 1 Advanced mode. SessionState stores the setup mode ('simple' | 'advanced', restored by reset and re-rendered on returning to Stage 1). Stage 2 in advanced mode adds three dropdown columns per archer row - Target face type (FACE_TYPES, readable names, default 10 zone), Face size (ADVANCED_FACE_SIZES_CM, default 60 cm) and Distance (the same Metric/Imperial optgroups as simple setup, default 20 yd) - and its intro explains that each archer has their own target; simple mode's Stage 2 is unchanged. Submitting parses and validates each row (a bad value names the row and the field, nothing is stored, the form is refilled) and stores each Archer with their own TargetSetup; the Event is built with target_setup=None. Stage 3, the overview and the match pages work unchanged on top of this. Switching Stage 1 back to Simple discards advanced per-archer data like any Stage 1 resubmission.
tests: Stage 1 renders Simple and Advanced radios, with Advanced no longer disabled and the submit button enabled in both modes; posting setup_mode=advanced stores 'advanced', builds the schedule and goes to Stage 2 (no TBA text anywhere in h2h/templates).
Returning to Stage 1 after choosing Advanced shows Advanced selected; after Reset it is back to Simple.

Stage 2 in advanced mode renders, per archer, a face-type select with exactly the FACE_TYPES options (default 10 zone), a face-size select with exactly the eight sizes (60 cm selected) and a distance select with the sixteen standard distances in Metric/Imperial optgroups (20 yd selected); in simple mode none of these appear.

Posting valid advanced rows stores each archer with their own TargetSetup, goes to Stage 3, and after confirming, event.target_for(i) is each archer's chosen face type/size/distance (e.g. 3 archers on 18 m 40 cm 10_zone, 50 m 122 cm 10_zone and 20 yd 60 cm Worcester).
An invalid face type, face size or distance in row 3 is rejected with a message naming row 3 and the field, stores nothing and refills every typed and selected value.

A full advanced-mode event with mixed targets (a 5-zone archer with maximum score 9 per arrow against a 10-zone archer) can be played from Stage 1 to the end over HTTP: scores above the 5-zone archer's maximum are rejected, the percentiles use each archer's own distribution, and the overview/results pages render.
Simple-mode behaviour is unchanged (existing Stage 1/2/3 tests pass, apart from the removed TBA tests which are replaced by the above).

Verified in a real browser: toggling Simple/Advanced on Stage 1 hides/shows the dropdowns and the note without disabling Continue; Stage 2 shows the three extra dropdowns per row in advanced mode; no JS console errors.
The full suite passes.

name: Chart data: every score each archer has shot, axis limits that include them, handicaps in the legend
description: Per Specification/feedback.md 'Feedback 5' (Graphs) and AISpec.md section 5.6 (Assumptions 31, 35): change h2h/chart_data.build_pair_chart_data. (1) Markers: instead of only the passes the two archers shared (the cause of the 'show previous passes' box adding no lines for later passes), the payload lists, for each archer, every scored pass of theirs against any opponent (including a bye pass shot alone), as `passes: [{index, score}]` ordered by pass, and the event's current pass index as `current_pass` (the pass shown by default). (2) Axis limits: x_min/x_max cover the trimmed curve range AND every score in both lists (not just the visible ones, so the axis does not move when the checkbox is ticked), with a margin of 1 score unit each side, clamped to [0, the larger of the two archers' maximum pass score]; curve points are listed over that final range. (3) Legend: each archer's payload entry carries a `legend` label of the form 'Name (handicap H)' (H shown as entered, 22.5 stays 22.5, 15.0 shows 15). (4) The distribution range and the maximum use each archer's own target maximum (Event.max_score_for) so pairs on different faces work. The pair page and the match page keep sharing this one function.
tests: Alice and Bob who met in pass 1 and then each faced someone else in passes 2 and 3: the payload for the pair (Alice, Bob) lists Alice's scores for passes 1, 2 and 3 and Bob's for 1, 2 and 3, each with its pass index, whichever opponent they were against; a pair that has never met has the same lists for their own passes.
A bye pass's score appears in that archer's list; an archer's passes they sat out do not.
`current_pass` is the event's current_rotation_index; an archer with no score yet in the current pass has no entry for it.

With a score far below the curves' trimmed range (e.g. 20 for a handicap-30 archer) and one far above, x_min <= min(all scores) - 1 and x_max >= max(all scores) + 1, both within [0, max pass score]; the range is identical whether or not the earlier passes are shown (it depends only on the full lists).
With every score inside the trimmed range the x-range equals the previous trimmed range (existing range tests pass) apart from the 1-unit margin where a score is near the edge.
Curve points are provided for every integer in the final [x_min, x_max] where the probability is non-zero.
`legend` is 'Name (handicap H)' with H as entered (22.5 -> 22.5, 15.0 -> 15).
For two archers on different targets (5-zone vs 10-zone, advanced mode) the payload's x_max never exceeds the larger maximum pass score and the y_max covers both distributions.
The payload is JSON-serialisable and the match page and pair page still render it; the existing chart-data tests are migrated and pass.

name: Outputs model: completed passes, leaderboard and per-archer results
description: Per Specification/feedback.md 'Feedback 5' (Outputs) and AISpec.md section 5.4a (Assumptions 36, 37, 38): add a Flask-free module h2h/outputs.py. Event gains completed_passes (the rotation indices in which every match is scored, in order; a partly scored pass is excluded until its last match is saved). outputs.leaderboard(event) returns one row per archer with rank, name, points (passes won among completed passes) and passes decided (completed passes in which the archer had an opponent), ordered by points descending then event order, with equal points sharing a rank (1, 2, 2, 4). outputs.archer_results(event) returns, for every archer in event order, the name, base handicap, total score (their scores over completed passes), a row per completed pass in which they shot (pass number as an integer starting at 1, opponent name or 'bye', score, percentile, equivalent handicap or None) and an averages row (mean score, mean percentile, mean handicap ignoring None, or None if there are none). Rows are plain dataclasses/tuples, easy to render as HTML, CSV or PDF.
tests: With no scored match, every archer has 0 points, 0 decided and rank 1 (all tied), and every per-archer table is empty with no averages.
With pass 1 fully scored and pass 2 half scored, only pass 1 contributes to points, totals and rows; saving pass 2's last match adds it; completed_passes is [0] then [0, 1].

Points equal the number of passes the archer won among completed passes (checked against the Event's results over a whole 4-archer event with known scores), and the sum of all points equals the number of decided paired matches.
Ranks are 1,2,2,4 for points 3,2,2,1; archers with equal points keep event order.
A bye (solo) pass adds no points, does not count as decided, and still gives that archer a results row with opponent 'bye'; a sit-out pass gives no row.
A per-archer table's rows are in pass order with 1-based pass numbers, the correct opponent name, score, percentile (0-1 fraction in the model) and handicap.

Total score is the sum of the rows' scores; the average row is the mean of the Score, Percentile and Handicap columns, ignoring a None handicap (score 0) in the handicap mean, and None for the handicap mean if every handicap is None.
An event that is mid-way through advancing shows the leaderboard consistent with the per-pass results (no match counted twice after a score is edited and re-saved).
The module imports without Flask and has docstrings on every function.

name: Results page leaderboard and per-archer results page

/event/archers has one section per archer with the heading 'name - total score N - handicap H' and a table whose headings are exactly Pass, Opponent, Score, Percentile, Handicap, plus an Average row as the last row; values equal outputs.archer_results.

The nav bar on every page links to /event/archers.

name: Exports: leaderboard and archer results as CSV, everything as PDF
description: Per Specification/feedback.md 'Feedback 5' (Outputs: exports to PDF or CSV of all, sensible formats) and AISpec.md section 5.4a (Assumption 39): add `fpdf2` as a dependency with `uv add fpdf2` (and `pypdf` as a dev dependency for tests; no pip) and a Flask-free module h2h/exports.py with leaderboard_csv(event), archer_results_csv(event) and results_pdf(event), all built from the task-52 outputs (so equally live and completed-passes-only). name: Handicap calculator: indoor/outdoor choice and every standard round
description: Per Specification/feedback.md 'Feedback 5' (Handicap Calculator) and AISpec.md section 5.5 (Assumption 40): rebuild the standalone calculator form. (1) Indoor/Outdoor radio buttons (default Indoor). (2) A round dropdown for the chosen kind: indoor = every round in archeryutils's AGB_indoor and WA_indoor sets, outdoor = every round in AGB_outdoor_imperial, AGB_outdoor_metric and WA_outdoor, each listed once by its archeryutils name (the compound variants '..._compound' / '..._compound_triple' are not listed separately), Portsmouth selected by default indoors and WA 70m (wa720_70) outdoors. Both lists are rendered and a small script shows the one that matches the radio button (and the compound checkbox only for Indoor), so the page also works with the right defaults when script is off. (3) The compound checkbox ('Shot with a compound bow', only shown indoors): for an indoor round it selects the compound variant of the chosen round where archeryutils has one and otherwise uses the same round; it is ignored for an outdoor round. The route reads the kind, round and compound flag, resolves the round by name from archeryutils itself, validates that the round belongs to the chosen kind's list (an unknown or wrong-kind round gives a friendly error, no result), and the page keeps the submitted choices after calculating. models.py replaces IndoorRound/resolve_indoor_round with a lookup over these sets (keeping the stats wrapper stats.handicap_for_round_score). The calculator remains independent of any event.
tests: The indoor list is exactly the non-compound rounds of AGB_indoor and WA_indoor (Portsmouth, WA 18m, Bray I, Stafford, Worcester, Vegas, Vegas 300, WA 25m ... and their triples) and the outdoor list exactly those of AGB_outdoor_imperial, AGB_outdoor_metric and WA_outdoor; no name ending in '_compound' or '_compound_triple' is listed; rounds appear once.

The page renders the Indoor/Outdoor radios (Indoor checked), both round dropdowns (Portsmouth selected indoors, WA 70m outdoors), the compound checkbox in a part of the page that is hidden when Outdoor is chosen, and a score box.

Indoor Portsmouth, not compound, score 560 gives the same handicap as archeryutils's handicap_from_score on portsmouth; with the compound box ticked it equals the value for portsmouth_compound and differs from the non-compound one; the same for WA 18m.

A round with no compound variant (Worcester, Vegas 300) with the compound box ticked gives the non-compound result and no error; a round whose variant exists (WA 25m, Bray II, Stafford, Vegas, triples) uses it.

An outdoor round (e.g. York or WA 1440 (90m)) with the compound box submitted (forced POST) ignores it and gives the plain round's result; an outdoor round with a typical score returns a sensible handicap to one decimal place.

A round name that is not in the chosen kind's list (e.g. an outdoor round with kind=indoor) or unknown gives the error message and no result; a score above the round's maximum or non-numeric gives the existing invalid-score message.
The submitted choices (kind, round, compound, score) are re-rendered after a result or an error.
Every indoor and outdoor round in the lists returns a finite handicap for a mid-range score (loop over all, no exceptions).
Verified in a real browser: switching Indoor/Outdoor swaps the dropdown and shows/hides the compound checkbox, calculating works for one indoor and one outdoor round; no JS console errors.
The existing calculator tests are migrated and the full suite passes.
